featured_reviews.name: Treesa Payyanat
featured_reviews.review_text:
Disclaimer: Please read the full review for a complete and honest perspective before forming an opinion.

The society is aesthetically beautiful and easily one of the best-looking societies in Marol, with a particularly stunning cliff view that adds to its charm.

However, my experience as a bachelor tenant was unfortunately quite unpleasant.

There appears to be a clear bias against bachelors, who are often treated as troublemakers without any valid reason. This starts with restrictive and inconsistent rules - such as bachelors not being allowed to keep plants on balconies while families are permitted to do so - and extends to being told not to walk around the society after midnight.

The most difficult part of my stay, however, was the landlord. She frequently went back on her word, which created ongoing stress and uncertainty. We were initially told she would be moving to a nearby society, but she ended up shifting just across the hall. There were also instances where she entered the house without proper notice, which felt like a serious invasion of privacy. The constant interference made it hard to truly feel at ease, despite our efforts to make the space feel like home.

Additionally, the security staff - particularly at the E-wing guard office - tended to excessively scrutinize bachelor residents, even when guests visited during the day.

Overall, while the infrastructure, views, and overall appearance of the society are commendable, the treatment of bachelor tenants and lack of respect for personal boundaries significantly impacted the living experience.

featured_reviews.name: Ashwin Umale
featured_reviews.review_text:
Good society with regular society activities. Mostly families stay here.

They have ample open space. But flats are congested and old. You will mostly see leakages or dampness on the walls during rainy season.

Swimming Pool is not operational.

For bachelor:
1) They have cool families how mind their own business
2) You have to pay 150 Rs/- per month for bike parking
3) 5000 Rs/- for move-in charges

Society security head is the worst person. He will create unnecessary fuss about anything and everything. Will keep a track of visitors at bachelor's house. Will keep saying that this is not allowed, that is not allowed (Note: We never created any rucus in the society).

Net net, he tries to get monthly money from you. If you pay him, he minds his own business, else he will keep poking you. He also takes commission from brokerage. Hence, he ensures that you don't renew your agreement soo that new people will move-in and he gets his commission.

If you can limit his nuisance, then it's a good society to stay in!

I was a tenant at Savannah Avalon Society, and I am compelled to share a very shameful and concerning issue happening here which no one seems to be addressing.

There is a supervisor named Manjrekar, who has been repeatedly misbehaving with female domestic workers (maids). He exploits his position for personal benefit, assigns them extra work if they “support” him, and takes advantage of knowing where the cameras are to hide his inappropriate actions. Many residents have witnessed him inappropriately touching maids and are aware of his character, yet no serious action has been taken against him.

It is deeply disappointing that such behavior is ignored by many, and people remain silent unless something extreme happens. This reflects poorly on the society’s management and residents who choose to look away instead of standing up for what is right.

Flats feel premium in terms of design and size

Better location advantage than Vasant Oasis & Blue Fortuna

Cons:

Security is extremely poor compared to Vasant Oasis & Blue Fortuna

Guards are rude, unprofessional, and often misbehave with residents and visitors

Frequent miscommunication and dishonesty by the security staff

Continuous inconvenience created for tenants, visitors, and delivery personnel

Building lacks amenities that other premium societies in the area offer

featured_reviews.name: Suprabha Shankari
featured_reviews.review_text:
*1/5 Stars - Worst Society: Not Tenant-Friendly*

I'm extremely disappointed with  savannah Avalon society, and would not recommend it to anyone. As a tenant, I've experienced numerous issues, including:

- Unresponsive management: Despite repeated complaints, the management has failed to address our concerns.
- Poor maintenance: The society's infrastructure is in disrepair, with frequent elevator breakdowns, leakages, and electrical issues.
- Lack of transparency: The society's finances and decision-making processes are opaque, leaving tenants in the dark.
- Unfair rules and regulations: The society has implemented arbitrary rules that is not at all tenant friendly, they won’t let us do yoga classes here

The society's attitude towards tenants is dismissive and uncooperative. They seem more interested in collecting maintenance fees than in providing basic services.

Unless you enjoy dealing with unnecessary stress and bureaucratic red tape, avoid [Savannah Avalon society] at all costs.

featured_reviews.name: Ravi Gupta
featured_reviews.review_text:
I am writing this review to genuinely warn anyone planning to visit or invest in the I Stay project in Marol, Andheri—please be extremely careful before going there.

My experience was very disappointing and honestly shocking. The sales team, including Niranjana and the team head Nikhil, is highly unprofessional and lacks even basic manners when dealing with customers. Instead of helping or explaining things properly, they speak in a rude and disrespectful tone.

When I tried to negotiate a small amount (₹1–2 lakhs), the response I received was insulting. Statements like “Is budget mein kabhi ghar liya hai kya?” clearly show how they judge customers based on money rather than treating them with respect.

Even worse, the information they provide is not trustworthy. In the sample flat, when I pointed out that the balcony and rooms were small, the salesperson casually said it was “by mistake” and would be bigger in the actual flat. If a sample flat—the main thing used to sell the project—is incorrect, how can any buyer trust what will actually be delivered?

The entire team seems to support this kind of behavior, so don’t expect professionalism from anyone there. Instead of guiding buyers, they come across as aggressive and argumentative, almost trying to pressure or dominate the conversation. This kind of experience is not what anyone expects when making such an important decision.

Buying a home is a serious investment, and no one should tolerate disrespect or misleading information. Customers are not there to prove their status—they are there to make one of the biggest decisions of their life.

Based on my experience, I strongly recommend avoiding this project and choosing more professional and trustworthy builders.

featured_reviews.review_text:
New tenants kindly read:

Me and my sister lived in this society for a good period, and overall, the environment and community are genuinely good peaceful locality and friendly neighbours. However, the experience during the vacating phase was extremely stressful and unpleasant due to the behaviour of the house owner.

Towards the end of my stay when it was time to vacate ( with proper 2months notice) and get the deposit back the owner became highly uncooperative, extremely rude, and unreasonable. There were unnecessary delays from his side, and he held my security deposit for nearly 50 days, causing a lot of mental stress.

Even though the house was handed over in good condition, he demanded extra repair work and complete house painting costing almost ₹25,000 none of which was ever mentioned in the rental agreement. These were completely unexpected and unfair expenses imposed at the last moment.

To add to this, Society members had already warned us about this owner’s behaviour, but unfortunately, we realised the seriousness of it only after facing the situation ourselves.

While the society overall is nice and the people are good, my experience with this particular owner, house : C4, was extremely unpleasant. I would not recommend renting under this owner, as the vacating process can become unnecessarily complicated, expensive, and mentally draining.

I am writing this review so that future tenants don’t face the same harassment that my sister and I had to go through.

featured_reviews.name: InfiniteBeastX4
featured_reviews.review_text:
This is one of the best apartments across Mumbai, however during my stay I was quite disappointed by the maintenance standards. Although the staff is really friendly and professional, they are also quite ignorant.

For example, there were multiple instances where there have been broken rocks/floors/nets/equipment near children's playing area, and they take weeks and weeks to get it repaired (that too after multiple complaints), or not repair it at all. Multiple children and people get hurt or trip over broken tiles yet the repairs are not prioritised. There have also been broken equipment in the gym, and despite multiple complaints they were not fixed.

Another major issue I experienced is their cheap cost cutting methods. They only turn on the common area air conditioning for barely 2 hours in the evening. There are people literally sweating during other busy times throughout the day but they still keep them totally off. We didn't ask for you to keep them on 24x7 but surely more than 2 hours across multiple times in the day would've really left a good impression for residents and visitors. Every single other high-range apartments I visited the main thing and first impression was always the air conditioned common area.

All residents pay a fortune for monthly maintenance, and these aforementioned things should be the least to expect. It has been over a year since I left the apartments so I don't know if things have improved, but if they are, I look forward to seeing your reply and steps taken.
